title: Optimize quantized kernels (INT8/FP8) and add smoothquant + dequant fusion for KV cache and continuous batching
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: Customers have seen uneven latency regressions when using INT8/FP8 quantized models with large KV-cache footprints and continuous batching. Root causes: redundant dequant/quant round trips in the attention path and suboptimal kernel layouts for mixed INT8/FP8 paths. Motivation: reduce p50/p99 token latency and per-token CPU/GPU cost without accuracy regressions. Changes: 1) Refactor quantized matmul and attention kernels to expose a fused dequant path that avoids allocating transient FP32 buffers when the downstream op can operate on fused scales; 2) Implement a smoothquant fusion pass that precomputes per-channel scaling and merges it into the quantized kernel execution to reduce quant->dequant overhead; 3) Add INT8/FP8 mixed-kernel codepaths optimized for continuous batching (reduced kernel launch overhead and better workspace reuse); 4) Introduce scheduling hints and KV-cache-aware batching decisions (prefer smaller batch windows for long-prefix streams to reduce p99 tail latency) and expose a config knob: runtime.kv_cache.fused_dequant=true; 5) Add microbenchmarks and regression harnesses and update docs/release notes. Benchmarks: internal perf suite (A100, H100, T4) shows median token latency down 18-27% on long-prefix streaming workloads and p99 down 12-22% with ~10-15% GPU memory footprint reduction for INT8 cases. Accuracy: end-to-end perplexity and downstream evals show negligible delta (<0.2% on our eval set) with provided compatibility tests. Testing: unit tests for fused kernels, integration tests that replay recorded streaming traces, and new perf CI job that runs lightweight kernel benchmarks on PR. Rollout: feature gate-off by default; staged rollout to Dedicated then Hosted with canary traffic; automated fallback to FP32 path if model-config mismatches or scale metadata absent. Notes: this PR touches low-level kernels and scheduling; follow-up work planned to extend fusion to rotary/rope scaling and to document operator-level contracts for third-party quantized models.

review_comments: Miguel Rivera: Left a few comments about edge-case rounding when per-channel scales are near-zero. Suggested adding a deterministic clamp to avoid NaN propagation in fp8->int8 paths.
Asha Patel: Responded: added clamp + unit test 'quant_scale_clamp' and documented behavior in kernel contract. Also added a fallback path that emits a warning when scale entropy is high.

Samir Kapoor: Asked about interactions with existing KV Cache eviction logic; recommended small scheduler change to prefer windowed batches for long prefix traces to reduce p99. Suggested a small E2E test simulating concurrent streams.
Asha Patel: Implemented scheduler hint 'prefer_small_windows_for_long_prefix' and added concurrent stream test in integration suite.
Evelyn Chen: Ran perf locally on H100 and asked for a microbenchmark breakdown by kernel (matmul vs attention). Noted an unexpected regression for tiny batch sizes on T4.

Asha Patel: Investigated and adjusted workspace reuse heuristics for small-batch T4 to avoid extra memcpy; added platform-specific heuristics in batching_controller. Re-ran benchmarks and updated PR with results.

release_notes: Performance: Reduced median token latency by 18-27% and p99 by 12-22% for INT8/FP8 quantized models on long-prefix streaming workloads via fused dequant + smoothquant fusion and kernel-level optimizations.
Feature: runtime.kv_cache.fused_dequant (off by default). When enabled, runtime will avoid transient dequant allocations for compatible models and use fused kernels for lower memory/latency.
Compatibility: No accuracy regressions observed in internal evals. Feature gated rollout with automatic FP32 fallback if model metadata missing.
summary: Optimizes quantized inference kernels (INT8/FP8) by fusing smoothquant and dequant paths and improving scheduling and continuous batching behavior for KV-cache heavy streaming workloads.
